office_does: One of 98 Washington State Representatives, serving two-year terms writing state law and the state budget for the 37th District (southeast Seattle, Skyway and part of Renton).
race_blurb: Open seat: Lavender Rights Project director Jaelynn Scott, a Democrat with a detailed progressive platform and endorsements from Bernie Sanders to the House Speaker, faces Independent college student Evon McCorkle. Scott took 88.3% in the primary.

candidates.summary: Executive Director of the Lavender Rights Project and self-described Democratic Socialist; would be Washington's first openly transgender legislator.
highlights: Says she redirected $16 million from jails into supportive housing [S1][S6]
Platform: wealth, capital-gains, corporate and high-earner taxes; a 5% rent-increase cap and social housing [S4]
Supports universal healthcare and defends abortion and gender-affirming care [S1][S4]
Community-based crisis response, independent police oversight and ending qualified immunity [S4]

taxes.basis: Calls for 'taxing the rich': corporate income, capital gains, wealth and high-earner payroll taxes.

spending.basis: Platform calls for universal childcare, universal healthcare, social housing and fully funded schools.

housing.basis: 'Housing is a human right, not a commodity': 5% rent cap, social housing, public and cooperative ownership, TOPA/COPA.

safety.basis: Community-based crisis response, independent police oversight, ending qualified immunity; redirected jail funding to housing.

experience.basis: No prior elected office, but a seven-year nonprofit executive with an organizational record.

immigration.basis: Platform: 'build a real sanctuary for Washington state.'

healthcare.basis: Supports universal healthcare with 'no deductibles, no debt' and the Washington Health Trust.

social.basis: Platform defends abortion and gender-affirming care; leads an organization serving Black trans communities.

tech.basis: Calls for ending mass surveillance and regulating and taxing data-center energy and water use.

candidates.summary: College student studying mathematics and physics and a first-time Independent candidate running on education, housing, healthcare and representation for working-class residents.
highlights: Says he is 'not backed by powerful insiders or political machines' [S1]
Priorities: education funding, housing affordability, affordable healthcare, 'fair tax reform' with financial responsibility [S4]
Has raised $700 and lists no endorsements [S3][S7]

experience.basis: College student and first-time candidate with no prior elected office.

reform.basis: Runs explicitly against 'powerful insiders or political machines' and on restoring trust in government, without specific reform proposals.
